sections.h2: Where is Dodge County, Georgia, and which towns does it hold?
sections.html:
Dodge County lies in the southern part of Georgia, mostly in the Ocmulgee River watershed, with Eastman as the county seat and largest city. Wikipedia gives a total area of 503 square miles, and the Census Bureau counts 495.96 square miles of land.

The legislature organized the county on October 26, 1870, carving it mostly from Laurens County with smaller pieces of Pulaski, Montgomery and Telfair. The Macon and Brunswick Railroad had been built the year before, and towns grew up along the line far from the old county seat at Hawkinsville. Chauncey, Eastman and Milan are cities. Chester and Rhine are towns, and Empire is a census-designated place that crosses into Bleckley County.

Highways include US 23, US 280, US 341 and the US 319 and 441 corridor, plus State Routes 46 and 117 and several others. The Heart of Georgia Regional Airport lies three miles east of Eastman on State Route 46 and houses an aviation campus of Middle Georgia State College. A seller in Dodge County is usually dealing with a rural or small-town parcel, and the county's own offices handle nearly every step.

sections.h2: Which Dodge County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The county's services directory lists the Tax Commissioner at 478-374-2154 and the Tax Assessors at 478-374-8122. The Board of Commissioners works from 643 Pearl Bates Avenue in Eastman, and the county's clerk of courts can be reached at 478-374-2871.

The Georgia Department of Revenue splits the work the same way in every county. The tax commissioner is the contact for paying a bill and, in most counties, for homestead filings. The assessors are the contact for the appraised value and for appeals. The county website has a Tax Payments link for paying online. The cities and towns inside the county publish these numbers:

  • Chauncey: 229-868-2296
  • Chester: 478-358-4550
  • Eastman: 478-374-7721
  • Milan: 229-362-4290
  • Rhine: 229-385-5521

If your house sits inside a city, ask both the county and the city clerk whether city tax comes on a separate bill.

sections.h2: When did the 2026 assessment appeal window close in Dodge County?
sections.html:
Dodge County mailed its 2026 tax assessment notices on June 19, 2026, and the last day to appeal was August 3, 2026. That window has passed for the 2026 digest, so a seller who missed it deals with the 2026 value as billed and watches for the next notice.

The county announcement says appeals could be filed by email, by U.S. mail, or online through the appeal module on the qPublic site. Anyone who did not receive a notice, or who has a question about one, was told to call the assessors at 478-374-8122. The notice arrives every year, and the 45 days run from the day it was mailed, so mark the mailing date when it comes.

The county also raised the processing fee for conservation use (CUVA), forest land protection (FLPA) and other preferential parcels to $30.00 for new, renewal and continuation covenants, effective July 1, 2025. Owners of farm or timber land should ask the assessors whether a covenant is recorded on the parcel before listing.

sections.h2: What are my appeal options once I file in Dodge County?
sections.html:
You choose one of three tracks on the state's uniform appeal form, and the form goes to the Dodge County Board of Tax Assessors, never to the state. The Department of Revenue cannot override a local value.

TrackWhat it coversWhat happens next
Board of EqualizationValue, uniformity, taxability or a denied exemptionAssessors may revise the notice; if not, a hearing is scheduled and a decision follows
Hearing officerValue or uniformity of non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000Decision, then superior court if still disputed
ArbitrationValue onlyTaxpayer submits a certified appraisal within 45 days of the acknowledgment; hearing scheduled within 30 days

Table source: Georgia Department of Revenue, Filing a Property Tax Appeal.

  • A superior court appeal needs a written notice filed with the assessors within 30 days of the decision
  • The county sends a settlement conference notice within 45 days of your notice of appeal
  • Taxes equal to the prior year's amount must be paid before the court will hear the case
  • A taxpayer who wins a value at 85 percent or less of the earlier figure can recover costs and attorney's fees

sections.h2: When are Dodge County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Georgia's default deadline is December 20, but a county can move it to December 1 or November 15, or bill in installments. The state also gives each owner 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest starts. Read the date printed on your Dodge bill, because it controls, and call the tax commissioner at 478-374-2154 if the bill is lost.

Delinquent balances can pick up penalties on top of interest. Ask the tax commissioner what your parcel owes before a closing, request the figure in writing, and give a copy to whoever runs the closing.

Returns of value are due between January 1 and April 1. An owner who paid taxes the prior year and files nothing is treated as having returned the same property at its last final value, so most homeowners never file a return.

sections.h2: Does Dodge County offer homestead exemptions?
sections.html:
Dodge County has no local homestead exemptions on top of the state's. A homeowner can still apply for the statewide homestead exemptions, and the Department of Revenue says an application can be made any time after the property becomes your primary residence, up to April 1 of the first year you want the benefit.

Failing to apply waives the exemption for that year. The state's standard exemption subtracts $2,000 from the assessed value, and assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value. The county's tax commissioner or assessors take the application, depending on how Dodge handles it, so ask which window to use.

A refund is possible for tax that was illegally or erroneously assessed and collected, but the claim must start within three years of payment. Georgia does not refund part of a year to someone who sells, because ownership on January 1 sets liability for the entire year.

sections.h2: How do taxes affect selling a house in Dodge County?
sections.html:
Whoever owned the parcel on January 1 owes that year's bill, so a sale in the fall still carries a full-year tax. The sales contract decides how the year is split, and the closing statement shows who pays what.

Two recorded items matter at closing. A security deed on a long-term loan must be recorded in the county within 90 days, and the intangible tax on it is $1.50 for every $500 of the note, collected by the clerk of superior court in most counties. A sale also triggers transfer tax, which the seller owes by law and which the Department of Revenue prints as $1 for the first $1,000 plus 10 cents for each added $100. County tax liens are filed on the general execution docket in the clerk's office, so a lien shows up in the title search.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Dodge County homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts the 2025 population at 19,663, down 1.7% from the April 2020 base, with 8,643 housing units and only 5 building permits issued in 2025.

  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 70.6%
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $118,100
  • Median gross rent: $723
  • Median household income: $51,587
  • Residents 65 and older: 20.8%
  • Population per square mile in 2020: 40.2

For comparison, the same table gives $357,800 for DeKalb County, so a Dodge County house sits at a much lower price point. Check the parcel's tax status before you list, since a back-tax balance weighs more against a lower sale price.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Dodge County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Dodge County Tax Commissioner at 478-374-2154. The Tax Assessors, at 478-374-8122, answer questions about values and appeals.

faqs.q: Is it too late to appeal my 2026 Dodge County assessment?
faqs.a: Yes for the 2026 digest. Notices were mailed June 19, 2026, and the last day to appeal was August 3, 2026. Watch for the next annual notice and count 45 days from its mailing date.

faqs.q: Does Dodge County have its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The Department of Revenue says Dodge has no local homestead exemptions, so owners apply for the statewide exemption through the county tax office by April 1 of the first year they want it.

faqs.q: When are Dodge County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The state default is December 20 unless the county sets another date or installments. Owners also get 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest. Use the date printed on your bill.

faqs.q: Can I get property tax back after selling my Dodge County house?
faqs.a: Georgia law does not refund a partial year, because the January 1 owner is liable for all of it. A refund is available only for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim within three years of payment.
